RECOMMENDED = Wide format (above). Pros: trivial for Shiny (one row per entity_key x date, direct columns for arearange; no pivot; backward compatible since new columns are additive and NA-safe). Cons: more columns; one column pair per level. Long format (value_type = Forecast-Mean/Lower/Upper + interval_level) is more normalized and matches the SQL source ValueType discriminator, but forces a pivot in Shiny and risks row-count x3 and join bugs. KEEP value_type column for upstream lineage even in wide format (it stays 'Forecast-Mean' for the mean row source); intervals live in dedicated numeric columns. Capping at zero (non-negative) should be a generation-side rule, not Shiny.
